designs.request_split: Randomise requests 50/50; both arms draw on the same partner volume
designs.budget_split: Randomise requests 50/50 and give each arm its own half of every partner's monthly volume
designs.region_split: Randomise postcode regions 50/50; partners serving both arms are shared
designs.switchback: Alternate the policy every 3 days, in random order; volume is shared

results.name: partner-shortage
results.about: Far more demand than partner capacity, so most requests compete for a small, quickly exhausted pool of partners.

results.name: partner-glut
results.about: Many more partners and much more capacity than the demand needs, so the question is which few partners each request should go to.

results.name: city-concentrated
results.about: Demand piles up in a few city regions while partner density follows it only weakly, leaving cities saturated and rural regions badly short.

results.name: wide-quality-spread
results.about: Partners differ far more in how often homeowners buy from them, how reliably they call and how fast, so picking the right partners matters much more.

results.name: ignored-leads
results.about: Partners on average call only about half the leads they buy, and slowly, so many homeowners risk never getting a call.

results.name: expensive-lead-mix
results.about: The category mix shifts toward high-price leads (real-estate sales and heat pumps), where each lead costs partners much more and wasted leads hurt profit.

results.name: frequent-pauses
results.about: About a third of partners pause for part of each month, so capacity seen in the history appears and disappears without warning.

results.name: hesitant-homeowners
results.about: Homeowners are far less ready to buy (about half the usual intent, fewer phone-qualified and fewer urgent requests), so few leads turn into projects.

floors.name: frontier.balanced.project_lift
floors.about: the model policy wins at least as many projects as the rules

floors.name: heldout.project_lift_share
floors.about: the model wins more projects than the rules in most blind worlds
